topic: How are pulsars formed? Pulsars are rotating neutron stars that produce pulses of radio waves, X-rays, and gamma rays. They form when a massive star runs out of fuel and collapses in on itself. The remnant is a neutron star with a strong magnetic field. The research should distinguish isolated magnetic-dipole spin-down from binary recycling and companion-ablation evolution, and test formation and evolution with mathematical models.

directions.title: Anisotropic Damping from Magnetic Inclination Decay: A Formal Analogy to Rotor Dynamics for Pulsar Spin-Down
directions.abstract: We resolve the missing assumption in isolated pulsar spin-down models by relaxing the constant magnetic inclination angle. By formally mapping the pulsar magnetic inclination angle alpha(t) to a rotor misalignment angle, we introduce its decay rate as an anisotropic damping term derived from the coupled electromagnetic torque equations. This yields a modified effective torque equation N(Omega) that naturally explains deviations of the braking index n_eff from 3 without invoking magnetic field decay. We formally derive the dominance condition under which this mechanism strictly bounds the validity domain in (P, Pdot, B) space, isolating it from multipole and wind braking confounders, and provide a protocol to ablate the damping term against binary recycling models.
